topics.name: Connectors: and, but, so, because, although

options: Every students has a water bottle.
Every student has a water bottle.
Every student have a water bottle.
questions.rule: Every is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb: every student has.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Baloo are eating all the honey.
Baloo is eat all the honey.
Baloo is eating all the honey.
questions.rule: Present continuous = is/am/are + -ing. One bear, so is eating.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the right connector.
options: Mowgli was tired, or he slept under a tree.
Mowgli was tired, so he slept under a tree.
Mowgli was tired, so he sleeped under a tree.
questions.rule: So shows a result: he was tired, so he slept. The past of sleep is slept.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: These points to more than one thing, so the noun must be plural: these books.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Loves is simple present with he/she, so the tag uses doesn't: doesn't he?
You always takes are: How are you doing?
Vines is plural and near (here), so use these.
A describing adjective comes before its noun: a brave panther.
I takes am, and the continuous form needs -ing: I am doing.

chat: It's a lovely day, isn't it?
options: Yes, it are. Let's go out.
Yes, it does. Let's go out.
Yes, it is. Let's go out.
questions.rule: Answer with the same helping verb as the tag: isn't it? - Yes, it is.

options: Either roads lead to the river.
Either road leads to the river.
Either road lead to the river.
questions.rule: Either means one of two, so use a singular noun and verb: either road leads.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: You will write to me, don't you?
You will write to me, won't you?
You will write to me, aren't you?
questions.rule: The tag repeats the helping verb in negative form: will becomes won't.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The second part is a result of the first, so join them with so.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: In a question with do/does, the main verb is in base form: Do you enjoy?

questions.before: I wanted to visit the jungle,
questions.rule: But joins two ideas that go against each other: wanted to visit, but it was far.
Each of + plural noun still takes a singular verb: each of the wolves has.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the present continuous.
questions.rule: Subject + is + verb-ing: Kaa is sleeping on the tree.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a question tag.
questions.rule: Positive sentence + negative tag: You like mangoes, don't you?

chat: Why didn't you come to the match?
options: I had a fever, so I stayed at home.
I had a fever, because I stayed at home.
I had a fever, so I stay at home.
questions.rule: Staying home is the result of the fever, so use so, and keep the past tense: stayed.
Singular one goes with singular this: this blue one.

options: Mowgli is an honest and active boy.
Mowgli is a honest and active boy.
Mowgli is an honest and actively boy.
questions.rule: Honest starts with a vowel sound, so use an. Before a noun use the adjective active, not the adverb.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: Shere Khan isn't friendly, isn't he?
Shere Khan isn't friendly, does he?
Shere Khan isn't friendly, is he?
questions.rule: A negative sentence takes a positive tag with the same verb: isn't ... is he?

options: Look! The monkeys is swinging from the vines.
Look! The monkeys swings from the vines.
Look! The monkeys are swinging from the vines.
questions.rule: Look! shows it is happening now, so use the present continuous; plural monkeys take are.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Every animal is singular, so the verb takes -s: knows.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Positive sentence with can takes the negative tag can't: can't he?

questions.after: Kaa looks scary, he is Mowgli's friend.
questions.rule: Although joins two ideas that seem to clash: he looks scary, yet he is a friend.

questions.after: a letter to her friend every month.
questions.rule: A habit (usually, every month) uses the simple present; with Radha (she) add -s: writes.

questions.prompt: Join the ideas in one sentence.
questions.rule: Cause first, then so + result: was hungry, so he ate bananas.

chat: You haven't visited the jungle yet, have you?
options: No, I don't. I will come next summer.
No, I haven't. I will come next summer.
No, I haven't. I will coming next summer.
questions.rule: Reply with the same helping verb: have you? - No, I haven't. After will use the base verb come.

chat: What is Baloo doing right now?
options: He is eating honey under a tree.
He are eating honey under a tree.
He is eat honey under a tree.
questions.rule: Right now needs the present continuous: He is eating.

options: Each of the girls have her own bicycle.
Each of the girl has her own bicycle.
Each of the girls has her own bicycle.
questions.rule: Each of the + plural noun (girls) + singular verb (has).

options: This children are playing with the wolf cubs.
These childs are playing with the wolf cubs.
These children are playing with the wolf cubs.
questions.rule: Children is the plural of child (not childs), and a plural noun takes these.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Yesterday and climbed show the past, so the reason after because is also past: wanted.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Comparing with the whole jungle needs the superlative: the longest.
Wrote is simple past, so the tag uses didn't: didn't she?
Honey is uncountable, so not many / a few. In questions we use any.
Distributive either + singular noun: Either path will take you home.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a question tag.
questions.rule: Positive is takes the negative tag isn't it?

chat: Do you still live near the river?
options: Yes, I does. I live there with the wolves.
Yes, I am. I live there with the wolves.
Yes, I do. I live there with the wolves.
questions.rule: A Do you ...? question gets a short answer with do: Yes, I do.

chat: Shall we practise in the morning or in the evening?
options: Either times are fine for me.
Either time is fine for me.
Either time are fine for me.
questions.rule: Either takes a singular noun and verb: either time is.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: There are three tigers near the river, aren't there?
There are three tigers near the river, aren't they?
There are three tigers near the river, isn't there?
questions.rule: With there are, the tag repeats there: aren't there?

options: Although the jungle is dangerous, but Mowgli feels safe there.
Although the jungle is dangerous, Mowgli feel safe there.
Although the jungle is dangerous, Mowgli feels safe there.
questions.rule: Use although OR but, never both in one sentence. Mowgli (he) takes feels.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Mowgli and Baloo both are two, so the plural verb is go.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The subject is each one (singular), so the verb is singular: is.

questions.before: Mowgli never gets lost in the jungle,
questions.rule: Never makes the sentence negative, so the tag is positive: does he?
Listen! means now, so use the present continuous. Somebody is singular: is singing.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a question tag.
questions.rule: Negative sentence (isn't) + positive tag (is he?).

questions.prompt: Join the ideas in one sentence.
questions.rule: Although + clause, comma, main clause: Although the river was deep, Mowgli swam across.

chat: I can't come to the city this year.
options: That's sad, but we can meet next year, can't us?
That's sad, but we can meets next year, can't we?
That's sad, but we can meet next year, can't we?
questions.rule: After can use the base verb meet; a positive sentence takes the negative tag can't we?

chat: How was the class picnic, Sana?
options: Every student enjoyed it, and the food was delicious.
Every students enjoyed it, and the food was delicious.
Every student enjoyed it, and the food were delicious.
questions.rule: Every + singular noun (student). Food is uncountable, so it takes was.
